text: A related list is how a form shows records from a completely different table — the records that point back at the one you have open, surfaced live at the bottom of the screen.

Chapter 3 covered reference fields — a field on one record pointing to another, like an Incident's Caller pointing at a row in the User table. A related list is that same relationship, read backwards. ServiceNow queries every Incident whose Caller points back at this user, and renders the result as a list at the bottom of the User's form. The Incident table still owns that data — you're looking at a live query result, not something stored on the User record.

An Incident form commonly carries several related lists: Affected CIs, showing configuration items this incident impacts from the CMDB; Related Problems, showing Problem records linked as this incident's root cause; and Approvals, tied to the incident's workflow. None of those records live inside the Incident table itself — each related list surfaces records from a different table, pre-filtered to the ones referencing the open incident.

A form's main fields describe the one record you opened. Related lists describe everything else that references that record, from other tables entirely, which is why they sit below the form fields, as their own tabbed or collapsible section. Scrolling to the bottom of an incident, you're not looking at more fields on that incident — you're looking at other records, on other tables, that happen to point back at it.

Related lists aren't fixed per table — they're configurable, the same philosophy forms and list columns follow. A Configure Related Lists option opens a picker showing every relationship ServiceNow can run against this table, letting you add, remove, or reorder which one appears first. That's how ServiceNow surfaces real one-to-many relationships without asking anyone to manually query a separate table.

Reference fields point forward; related lists are that same relationship read backwards, surfaced live at the bottom of a form. Next up: a worked lab pulling form layout, list layout, filters, and related lists together into one realistic task.
